subject: Throughput guardrails and reserved commit structure for Dedicated
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya@acme-ai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-ai.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit — throughput guarantees & measurement approach

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked Redwood's dedicated capacity model; it maps well to our low-latency inference needs. Before procurement can approve a reserved commit, procurement and engineering asked for a crisp statement of:

- tokens/sec and requests/sec guarantees we can expect at each commit band
- latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and how you measure them
- what acceptance tests you run during onboarding and what evidence we will get

We have a target of ~100k tokens/sec sustained (across the pool) for our highest band, with p95 tail latency <= 300ms for 256-token responses. We also care about cold-cache behavior for burst windows.

Can you share the proposed measurement methodology and whether pricing discounts change if we require higher guaranteed throughput?

Also attaching a small sample of our payload characteristics (acme-workload-sample.json).

Best,
Priya
Priya Desai
Head of Platform, Acme AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput guarantees & measurement approach

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask and for the payload sample. Quick summary up front: we can describe guarantees in two dimensions (committed sustained throughput + allowed burst) and provide a formal acceptance test for onboarding. Pricing/discounts are tiered by commit band and by whether you want guaranteed tokens/sec (hard SLA) vs best-effort target.

Below are the key items we typically propose; I’ve included an outline of the measurement methodology and the tradeoffs that affect discounts. We can lock down numbers once we align on the test harness (synthetic vs replay).

Proposed elements:
- Commit bands: Bronze / Silver / Gold mapped to sustained tokens/sec across pool (e.g., 25k / 75k / 150k)
- Burst allowance: 1.5x sustained for up to 60s, subject to GPU availability and queueing policies
- Latency targets: p50/p95/p99 measured at request level for 256-token responses (configurable). Default targets we propose: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 700ms (for Gold band under sustained load)
- Measurement methodology: hybrid replay + live sampling. Key factors: warm vs cold cache, KV cache enabled, model variant, sequence length distribution.

Discount/price notes:
- Standard reserved commit discounts apply to Bronze/Silver; Gold with hard SLA (money-back credits for missed rate) requires a minimum 12-month commit and a higher upfront commit.
- If Acme requests higher guaranteed sustained throughput than our Gold band, pricing will be custom (additional GPU pool + higher commit) — we can run a sizing exercise once we finalize your P95/P99 latency targets and expected token mix.

Acceptance tests and evidence:
- We provide: (1) benchmark run report (tokens/sec, requests/sec, latency distribution), (2) raw logs and traces for the test window, (3) a short recording of console dashboards.
- Measurement period: 30-minute sustained run + five 60s burst windows (default). We compare to a replay of a production-shaped request stream (you provided a sample; we will expand it).

Next steps:
1) Karthik — can you propose initial commit bands and a mapping to GPU pool sizing based on Acme sample?
2) Monica — I'll share a redlined SLA draft that includes the measurement acceptance criteria and credit policy.

I'll also attach our SLA draft for your team to review.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput guarantees & measurement approach

Hi Priya — I pulled in a quick sizing pass after looking at your sample. High-level notes:

- Your sample is ~40 tokens per request on average with modest variance. At 100k tokens/sec sustained that maps to ~2.5k r/s (requests/sec).
- For our current GPU families and the model variant you referenced, a Gold-equivalent pool for 100k sustained tokens/sec typically requires 8 x A100-80GB-equivalent slots with our optimized runtime (with KV caching enabled and continuous batching tuned). That assumes a warm cache.
- Cold-cache startup adds ~15–25% CPU/GPU overhead for the first minute; we account for that in burst allowance but not in sustained rate.

Measurement specifics we propose for the acceptance test:
1) Replay harness: we will run a replay of a representative 30-minute sample derived from your file (we will syntheticize timestamps to produce sustained load).
2) Tooling: we run rbench-v2 (internal) which measures tokens/sec, requests/sec, and latency histograms per 10s window.
3) Warmup: 10-minute warmup before the measurement window.
4) Burst tests: three 60s bursts at 1.5x sustained with 2-minute cool-down.
5) Pass criteria: sustained tokens/sec >= agreed band for >= 95% of 10s windows during the measurement window; p95 latency <= agreed target.

Pricing/clawback: if the test fails to hit sustained throughput we will offer an operational remediation plan; credits for SLA misses are capped and tiered (details in SLA).

If you'd like I can model alternative sizing for 150k sustained as well — it scales roughly linearly in GPU slots (so ~12 slots for 150k, ballpark).

-Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — that sizing math is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from our infra team before we proceed to procurement: 

1) For the acceptance test, will the replay be exactly your rbench-generated traffic or will you replay our sample verbatim? We care about models of user behavior (burstiness) being preserved.
2) On p95 latency: is that measured across the whole pool (global p95) or per-GPU-worker p95? We need the metric to reflect user experience (global).
3) If we accept a Gold band with a hard SLA, what is the typical lead time to provision the pool? Our timeline is 6 weeks.

Also procurement asked if we could get a small pilot (2-week) at Silver pricing but with the option to escalate to Gold commit with a credit for the pilot period applied to the commit if we convert. Would that be possible?

Best,
Priya

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acme-ai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput guarantees & measurement approach

Hi Priya — quick answers inline: 

1) Replay approach: we do a hybrid. We will run your sample verbatim for a subset of the run to preserve burst patterns (you pick a 10-minute window that matters), and rbench will synthesize the sustained part to match overall token/request distributions. That gives us reproducible load while keeping your real burst characteristics.
2) p95 measurement: we report both per-worker and global p95. For the SLA we use global p95 (user-facing) computed from ingress timestamps aggregated across the pool.
3) Lead time: Gold pool provisioning is typically 4–8 weeks depending on region and slot availability; 6 weeks is feasible if we have PO/commit by the end of next week.

Pilot ask: we can do a 2-week pilot at Silver pricing. Terms: pilot runs as an evaluation license (no SLA credits) but we can apply 50% of the pilot invoice toward the first month of a Gold commit if you convert within 30 days. That concession requires acceptance of an MoU (simple agreement) and a short statement of work.

If that sounds good we can: (a) update the SLA to include pilot->commit credit language, (b) schedule a sizing verification run next Tuesday. Rishi, I’ve drafted the MoU language into the SLA PDF — see page 3.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Account Ops, Redwood Inference
